examples.en: The company rushed a technician to the site.
They say the government rushed a rescue team to the area.
We have to send a reporter urgently to the scene.
The head office decided to send staff urgently.
The team that was rushed there arrived late at night.

examples.ko: 지원 인력을 급파하면 피해를 줄일 수 있어요.
examples.en: If we send support staff right away, we can reduce the damage.

explain: '보내다'보다 훨씬 급하게, 긴급한 일을 해결하러 사람을 보낼 때 써요. 주로 뉴스나 회사 업무에서 쓰고, 보내는 대상은 보통 사람이나 팀이에요.

phrases.en: The company rushed a repair technician to the site.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 생긴 곳으로 사람을 급하게 보낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when sending someone in a hurry to where something happened.

phrases.en: Firefighters were dispatched to the site of the fire.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피동 형태로, 보내진 사람을 주어로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, used when the sent people are the subject.

phrases.en: The broadcaster rushed a reporter to the accident scene.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 자주 들리는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing often heard in the news.

explain_en: It is much more urgent than '보내다' (to send) and is used when sending people to deal with an emergency. It mainly appears in news and business, and the object is usually a person or team.

examples.en: The thief fled in a hurry when he saw the police.

examples.ko: 차를 타고 도주하는 범인을 쫓고 있어요.
examples.en: They are chasing the criminal who is fleeing by car.
The driver who caused an accident and ran off was caught.
We still don't know where the culprit ran off to.
The person who tried to flee was caught at the door.

examples.ko: 그는 밤을 틈타 도주할 계획을 세웠어요.
examples.en: He made a plan to escape under cover of night.

explain: 주로 범인이 잡히지 않으려고 도망갈 때 쓰는 딱딱한 말이라서 뉴스에 자주 나와요. 일상에서 도망갈 때는 '도망가다'나 '튀다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. '뺑소니'는 사고를 내고 달아나는 것만 가리켜요.

phrases.en: The thief ran away when he saw the police.
phrases.nuance_ko: '도주하다'보다 일상 대화에서 훨씬 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Much more natural than 도주하다 in everyday speech.

phrases.en: The criminal who fled has not been caught yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 '달아난 범인'을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in news for a criminal on the run.

phrases.en: The suspect is still on the run.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 달아나고 있는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes someone who is still fleeing.

explain_en: It is a formal word mostly used when a criminal runs to avoid capture, so it appears often in the news. In daily life, 도망가다 or the slangy 튀다 sounds far more natural. 뺑소니 refers only to a hit-and-run.

t90.ax: He made a plan to escape under cover of night.

en: not running for office; giving up candidacy

examples.ko: 그 의원은 다음 선거에 불출마를 선언했어요.
examples.en: That lawmaker announced he won't run in the next election.
His supporters were quite disappointed by the news that he won't run.
Opinions were divided over the choice not to run.

examples.ko: 그가 불출마로 마음을 굳혔다는 기사가 났어요.
examples.en: An article said he had made up his mind not to run.
His decision not to run changed the shape of the election.

examples.ko: 대표는 불출마 결정을 내리기까지 오래 고민했어요.
examples.en: The leader thought long and hard before deciding not to run.

explain: 선거에 후보로 나가는 것은 '출마'이고, 나가지 않겠다는 뜻이 '불출마'예요. 정치 뉴스에서 '출마 선언'의 반대로 '불출마 선언'이라는 말이 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The lawmaker declared he would not run at the press conference.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선거에 나가지 않겠다고 공식적으로 밝힐 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for officially announcing you won't run in an election.

phrases.example: 시장은 다음 선거에 불출마 의사를 밝혔어요.
phrases.en: The mayor made clear his intention not to run in the next election.
phrases.nuance_ko: '선언'보다 조금 부드럽게 마음을 알릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A slightly softer way to state one's intent than 선언 (declare).
phrases.en_equiv: to state an intention not to run

phrases.en: Everyone was surprised by the sudden decision not to run.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나가지 않기로 정한 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the outcome of deciding not to run.

explain_en: Entering an election as a candidate is '출마', and choosing not to is '불출마'. In political news, '불출마 선언' often appears as the opposite of '출마 선언'.

examples.ko: 나라는 잃었던 땅의 수복을 간절히 바랐어요.
examples.en: The country earnestly hoped for the recovery of its lost land.

examples.ko: 도시 수복 소식에 사람들이 모두 기뻐했어요.
examples.en: Everyone was delighted at the news of the city's recapture.

examples.ko: 그 지역의 수복이 자꾸 늦어지고 있어요.
examples.en: The recovery of that region keeps getting delayed.
After the recovery succeeded, the residents came back.

examples.ko: 이 지역의 수복은 오래전부터 큰 숙원이었어요.
examples.en: Recovering this region has long been a great wish.

examples.ko: 수복 작업도 이제 거의 끝나 가요.
examples.en: The recovery work is almost finished now.

explain: 잃었던 땅이나 지역을 되찾는 일을 말하고, 주로 역사나 뉴스에서 나와요. 몸이 나아지는 건 '회복', 낡은 것을 원래대로 되살리는 건 '복원'이라고 해서 쓰임이 달라요. 일상 대화에서는 '되찾기'라고 풀어서 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.example: 전쟁이 끝난 뒤 영토 수복이 가장 큰 목표였어요.
phrases.en: After the war, recovering the territory was the biggest goal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잃은 땅을 되찾는 일을 말할 때 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for taking back lost land.

phrases.en: The army succeeded in retaking the city.
phrases.nuance_ko: 되찾는 일이 잘 끝났다는 뜻으로 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in news to say the retaking was successful.

phrases.en: The recapture operation ended in three days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군사 이야기에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in military contexts.

explain_en: It is the act of getting back lost land or territory, and it mostly appears in history and the news. Getting better physically is '회복' and restoring something old to its original state is '복원', so the uses differ. In daily talk people often say '되찾기' instead.

t90.ax: The recovery work is almost finished now.

en: to die in the line of duty

examples.ko: 화재 현장에서 구조하다 순직한 소방관을 추모했어요.
examples.en: We paid tribute to the firefighter who died in the line of duty during a rescue at a fire.
He died in the line of duty in an accident while on duty.

examples.ko: 군인이 훈련 중에 순직하면 국가가 예우해요.
examples.en: If a soldier dies in the line of duty during training, the state honors them.

examples.ko: 순직하신 선생님을 기리는 비석이 학교에 세워졌어요.
examples.en: A memorial stone honoring the teacher who died on duty was set up at the school.

examples.ko: 일하다가 순직했다는 뉴스를 보고 마음이 아팠어요.
examples.en: I felt sad when I saw the news that someone died on duty.

examples.ko: 순직하는 공무원이 없도록 안전 장비를 늘려야 해요.
examples.en: We need more safety equipment so that no public servant dies in the line of duty.

explain: 소방관, 경찰, 군인, 교사 같은 공무원이 맡은 일을 하다가 목숨을 잃는 것을 높여 말하는 표현이에요. 보통 회사원이 일하다 사고로 죽었을 때는 '사망했다'고 하고, 높여 말할 때는 '순직하셨다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: That police officer died in the line of duty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돌아가신 분을 높이는 말로, 뉴스나 추모할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An honorific form used in the news and in memorials.
phrases.en_equiv: died in the line of duty (honorific)

phrases.en: A memorial was held for the firefighters who died on duty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 붙여 누구인지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a noun to say who it is.
phrases.en_equiv: a firefighter who died on duty

phrases.en: This is a park honoring those who died on duty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일하다 목숨을 잃은 사람들을 한꺼번에 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for people who lost their lives on duty.

explain_en: This is a respectful word for losing one's life while doing one's duty, typically as a public servant such as a firefighter, police officer, soldier or teacher. For an ordinary office worker who dies in a workplace accident, people usually say '사망했다'. To show respect, say '순직하셨다'.

en: to be closed; to be blocked

examples.en: The road was closed because of an accident.
That factory was shut down last year.
The gate is closed off, so we can't get in.
If the park is closed, where will we exercise?
I don't know why my account was closed.
There is a school that will be closed down next month.

explain: '닫히다'는 문이 닫히는 가벼운 말이고, 폐쇄되다는 공식적으로 또는 오랫동안 막힌다는 뜻이에요. 도로, 공장, 학교, 계정처럼 큰 대상에 써요. 가게가 문을 닫는 것은 '폐업하다'를 더 많이 말해요.

phrases.example: 폐쇄된 도로라서 다른 길로 가야 해요.
phrases.en: The road is closed, so we have to take another route.
phrases.nuance_ko: '폐쇄되다'를 뒤의 말을 꾸미는 모양으로 바꾼 것으로, 막힌 길이나 시설을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifying form, referring to a blocked road or facility.

phrases.en: The bridge is closed because of construction.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 막혀 있는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe something that is currently closed off.

phrases.en: I was surprised that the school suddenly closed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예상하지 못하게 막혔다는 느낌을 더하는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing that adds the sense of an unexpected shutdown.

explain_en: '닫히다' is the light word for a door closing, while 폐쇄되다 means being shut officially or for a long time. It suits big things like roads, factories, schools, and accounts. A shop going out of business is more often '폐업하다'.

t90.ax: That factory was shut down last year.

examples.en: The city closed the dangerous bridge.
I hear the company is shutting down the regional factory.
They decided to close the school down.
The police are sealing off the accident site.
If you close the account, all the data disappears.
They sealed the entrance, so no one can leave.

explain: '닫다'보다 공식적이고 크게 막는다는 느낌이에요. 가게는 '폐업하다', 학교는 '폐교하다'처럼 대상마다 따로 쓰는 말도 있어요. 반대말은 '개방하다'예요.

phrases.en: The company shut down the accounts that weren't in use.
phrases.nuance_ko: 온라인 계정을 공식적으로 막을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for officially closing an online account.

phrases.en: They closed the road because of construction.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 지나가지 못하게 막을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for blocking a road so people cannot pass.

phrases.en: The city plans to close down the old building.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 닫을 계획을 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An expression used to state a plan to close something.

explain_en: It feels more official and larger in scale than '닫다'. Some targets have their own words, like '폐업하다' for a shop and '폐교하다' for a school. The opposite is '개방하다'.

p.n: 폐쇄시키다 stresses that someone made or ordered it to be shut.

en: to disband; to dissolve; to break up

examples.en: The agency decided to disband the group.
The workers took down the old building.
I took the watch apart and examined its parts.
The boss is trying to disband the team.
If you dissolve the company, the employees lose their jobs.

examples.ko: 책상을 해체하는 데 한 시간이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took an hour to take the desk apart.

explain: '해체하다'는 팀이나 그룹을 끝내는 것부터 기계나 구조물을 뜯는 것까지 넓게 써요. 기계나 가구를 부품으로 나눌 때는 '분해하다', 건물을 없앨 때는 '철거하다'가 더 구체적이에요. 모임을 끝내고 흩어지게 할 때는 '해산하다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 회사는 적자 때문에 팀을 해체하기로 했어요.
phrases.en: The company decided to disband the team because of losses.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조직을 끝낼 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for ending an organization.

phrases.en: I took the broken watch apart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계나 가구를 부품으로 나눌 때 더 구체적으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: More specific for splitting a machine or furniture into parts.

phrases.en: The city hall decided to tear down the old bridge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물이나 시설을 없앨 때 더 구체적으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: More specific for removing a building or facility.

explain_en: 해체하다 covers a wide range, from ending a team or group to taking apart machines or structures. For splitting a machine or furniture into parts, 분해하다 is more specific, and for tearing down a building, 철거하다. To end a gathering and send people away, use 해산하다.

en: to be very grateful; to be very thankful

examples.en: I thought I'd be more than grateful just to be given an interview.

examples.ko: 표를 구해 주신 것만 해도 감지덕지인데 밥까지 사 주시다니요.
examples.en: I'm already so grateful that you got me a ticket, and now you're even buying me a meal!
I'm just thankful to get my pay on time.

examples.ko: 이렇게 좋은 방을 싸게 빌려주시니 감지덕지할 따름이에요.
examples.en: You're renting me such a nice room so cheaply, I can't thank you enough.

examples.ko: 친구가 차로 데려다 주겠다고 해서 감지덕지했어요.
examples.en: My friend offered to drive me there, and I was really grateful.
Wouldn't you be happy with a result like that?

explain: 기대가 크지 않았는데 그것만으로도 고맙고 만족스럽다는 느낌이에요. 그래서 '~만 해도 감지덕지', '~면 감지덕지'처럼 자주 말해요. 그냥 '고맙다'보다 '이 정도도 과분하다'는 뉘앙스가 있어요.

phrases.en: Just getting paid on time is more than I hoped for.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기대가 크지 않아서 이 정도도 고맙다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means being thankful for even this little because expectations were low.

phrases.en: I'd be grateful for even a small discount.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)면 감지덕지'는 부탁할 때 공손하게 낮추어 말하는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-(으)면 감지덕지' is a humble form used when asking politely.

phrases.en: I'm just grateful to have a seat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사로 활용해 지금 상황에 만족하고 고마워한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a verb to say you are content and grateful with the situation.
phrases.en_equiv: to be grateful for even a little

explain_en: It carries the feeling that you expected little, so even this much is more than enough. People often say '~만 해도 감지덕지' or '~면 감지덕지'. Compared with a plain '고맙다', it implies 'even this is more than I deserve'.

en: seeing something makes you want it

examples.ko: 견물생심이라고, 가게에서 예쁜 걸 보니 사고 싶어졌어요.
examples.en: They say seeing breeds wanting: I saw something pretty in the shop and wanted to buy it.
Seeing makes you want things, so I left my wallet at home.
As the saying goes, once you see it you want it, and my spending goes up whenever I go to the mall.
Wanting what you see is a feeling everyone has.

examples.ko: 견물생심이 무서워서 비싼 가게는 안 가요.
examples.en: I'm afraid of wanting things when I see them, so I don't go to expensive stores.

examples.ko: 아이들은 견물생심으로 장난감 가게 앞을 못 떠나요.
examples.en: The kids want everything they see and can't leave the front of the toy store.

explain: 물건을 직접 보면 갖고 싶은 마음이 생긴다는 말이에요. 쇼핑이나 충동구매 이야기에서 가볍게 쓰고, '견물생심이라고'처럼 인용하는 모양으로 자주 말해요. 영어의 'opportunity makes the thief'와 완전히 같지는 않고, 보면 욕심이 생긴다는 쪽에 가까워요.

phrases.example: 견물생심이죠, 예쁜 옷을 보면 사고 싶어져요.
phrases.en: That's how it is; when you see pretty clothes, you want to buy them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대 말에 공감하며 가볍게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used lightly to agree with what someone said.

phrases.example: 견물생심이라서 마트에 가면 늘 많이 사요.
phrases.en: Seeing things makes me want them, so I always buy a lot at the mart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말할 때 '-이라서'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-이라서' to give a reason.

phrases.en: When I see something pretty, I start to want it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '견물생심' 대신 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday talk, people say this instead of 견물생심.
phrases.en_equiv: to want it once you see it

explain_en: It says that when you actually see something, you start to want it. It is used lightly in talk about shopping and impulse buying, often in a quoting form like '견물생심이라고'. It is not exactly the same as 'opportunity makes the thief'; it is closer to 'seeing it makes you want it'.

en: to be elated; to be puffed up

examples.ko: 시험에서 일등을 한 뒤로 그 친구는 기고만장해요.
examples.en: Ever since he came first on the exam, that friend has been full of himself.
Don't get too cocky just because you were praised a little.

examples.ko: 승진하고 나서 기고만장한 모습이 보기 안 좋아요.
examples.en: He looks cocky since his promotion, and it's not a good look.

examples.ko: 형은 한 번 이기면 금방 기고만장해져요.
examples.en: My older brother gets cocky as soon as he wins once.
The person who was so full of himself is quiet these days.
I was talking all puffed up and ended up making a mistake.

explain: 잘난 척하고 우쭐대는 부정적인 느낌이 강해서, 보통 다른 사람을 보며 '너무 기고만장하다'고 말해요. '기세등등하다'와 비슷하지만 '기고만장하다'가 더 잘난 척하는 느낌이에요. '기고만장해지다'처럼 변화를 나타내는 말로도 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 그는 이기고 나서 기고만장한 표정을 지었어요.
phrases.en: After winning, he put on a cocky expression.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우쭐대는 얼굴이나 태도를 꾸며 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a smug face or attitude.

phrases.en: After hearing praise a few times, he got cocky.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거에 점점 우쭐해진 변화를 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows a change into becoming puffed up in the past.

phrases.en: That player doesn't get cocky even after winning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로, 잘돼도 겸손하다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used to praise someone as humble even when doing well.

explain_en: It carries a negative feeling of showing off and getting cocky, so people usually say it about someone else. It is close to '기세등등하다', but '기고만장하다' feels more arrogant. You can also use it for change, as in '기고만장해지다' (to become cocky).

t90.ax: My older brother gets cocky as soon as he wins once.

en: to be unsure; to be dubious

examples.en: I'm not sure this is the right way.
I'm still not sure whether that story is true.
I wasn't sure, so I asked once more.
I can't tell if the answer is number 3 or 4.

examples.ko: 그 사람을 아는 것 같기도 하고 아닌 것 같기도 해서 긴가민가했어요.
examples.en: I felt I might know him, or might not, so I wasn't sure.
If you're not sure, check first.

explain: 확실하지 않아서 판단이 안 설 때 쓰는 말로, 말할 때 많이 써요. 비슷한 '헷갈리다'는 둘 이상이 섞여 구별이 안 될 때, '긴가민가하다'는 맞는지 아닌지 모를 때 써요. '맞는지', '사실인지' 같은 말과 자주 같이 나와요.

phrases.en: At first, I wasn't sure whether that was true.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 지나간 때의 불확실한 마음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about uncertainty you felt in the past.

phrases.en: My friend looked at me with an unsure expression.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때는 '긴가민가한'으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '긴가민가한' when modifying a noun.

phrases.en: I'm not sure, but I'll give it a try.
phrases.nuance_ko: 확실하진 않아도 일단 해 본다고 말할 때 연결해 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you'll try something even though you're not certain.

explain_en: It is a spoken-style word for when you can't decide because you aren't certain. '헷갈리다' is for when things get mixed up and you can't tell them apart, while '긴가민가하다' is for not knowing whether something is true or not. It often follows clauses like '맞는지' or '사실인지'.

examples.en: The children play, laughing and giggling.
The baby giggled because it tickled.

examples.ko: 친구들이 제 이야기를 듣고 까르르 웃음을 터뜨렸어요.
examples.en: My friends heard my story and burst into giggles.

examples.ko: 교실 뒤쪽에서 까르르 웃는 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: I can hear giggling from the back of the classroom.
The students passed by, giggling.

examples.ko: 동생이 영상을 보더니 까르르 웃기 시작했어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling watched the video and started giggling.

explain: 주로 아이나 젊은 사람들이 내는 맑고 높은 웃음소리를 나타내요. 거의 '웃다'와 함께 '까르르 웃다'로 써요. 낮고 거친 웃음소리에는 어울리지 않아요.

phrases.en: I can hear giggling from the next room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '웃는 소리'와 함께 써서 웃음소리를 구체적으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with 웃는 소리 to describe the sound of laughter specifically.

phrases.example: 친구 말에 모두 까르르 웃음이 터졌어요.
phrases.en: Everyone burst into giggles at my friend's words.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 웃음이 나오는 순간을 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows the moment laughter suddenly breaks out.

phrases.en: The babies are giggling again and again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반복해서 쓰면 웃음이 계속 이어지는 느낌이 더 커져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Repeating it makes the continuous laughter feel stronger.

explain_en: It describes the clear, high-pitched laughter of children or young people. It is almost always used with '웃다' as '까르르 웃다'. It does not suit a low or rough laugh.
